about: A temporary camera (docs/API.md, Temporary cameras; docs/WEB-CAMERA.md § 3): a browser's page that shows a room to a home's devices for a day, a week at most, without ever holding a key of the home's. The member that approves it draws 32 random bytes for it alone, the camera's secret; from it come a signal key, a box key and a media key, by the derivation an epoch's secret uses (keys-v1.json). Everything the camera and the home's devices say to each other is sealed and signed in today's formats (sealed-v1.json) under those keys, with the home's epoch when the camera started written into each.

It gets in by a camera invite: the invite's protocol whole (invite-v1.json: the proof, the commitments, the member nonce, the code, the approval's MAC), with the token sealed for the household under a context of its own ("petcam.caminvite.v1|<invite id>") with its kind inside, so a build from before temporary cameras can't open it and so can never hand the home's keys over for it. Approving one hands over a pass in a keyring's place.

The pass is wrapped as a keyring is (keyring-v1.json): HPKE (RFC 9180) in auth mode, DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, from the approving device's key to the page's; info "petcam.campass.v1"; associated data "petcam.campass.v1|<household id>|<camera id>|<epoch>". It travels as "<encapsulated key>.<ciphertext and tag>", both base64url. Inside is snake_case JSON with its bytes as base64url, like everything on the wire but a keyring's inside.

The entry is what the home's members know the camera by: its secret and the rest, sealed as any message (0x04) with the home's box key, bound to "petcam.tempcam.v1|<household id>|<camera id>". It opens only under the home's current keys.

`expect` is "opens" (for taking a pass, "takes"), or how it fails: "refused" (it doesn't authenticate, or isn't what it should be inside), "stale_keys" (an older epoch than the home's current one), "newer_keys" (a newer one: catch up on the home's keys, then look again), "unknown_keys" (another epoch than the one it must name), "over" (past its end).

Sealing draws a random nonce and HPKE a random ephemeral key; the ones here are fixed, each derived from its vector's name, so an implementation given them gets the same bytes. JSON is compared as values, never as text.

CryptoKit draws its own ephemeral key, so what it seals differs every time: `pass.sealed_by_cryptokit` was sealed once by SharedTests/TemporaryCameraVectorTests.swift and recorded (server/scripts/vectors/recorded/cryptokit-pass.json). The Apple apps are who make passes, so a page has to open these.
Bytes are base64url without padding unless a field says hex or base64; strings are UTF-8; "|" joins the parts of a message, with nothing around it.
HKDF is HKDF-SHA256 with salt "petcam" and 32 bytes out; HMAC is HMAC-SHA256; AES-GCM is AES-256-GCM with a 12-byte nonce and a 16-byte tag.

Made by server/scripts/vectors.mjs from fixed keys that were made up for these files; nothing here was ever a real home's. No vector is ever removed: a format the apps stop opening stays, as one that must fail. The page's address here, https://camera.example/petcam/, is no real host's. Read by SharedTests/TemporaryCameraVectorTests.swift, server/test/vectors.test.ts and android/core's TemporaryCameraVectorTest.kt.

holders.how: Which epochs each device here holds. Its current epoch is its newest. The camera starts while the home is at epoch 1.

member.what: a viewer in the home: it makes the invite, approves the page, wraps the pass and seals the entry

page.what: the page's own key pair, which a browser holds so it can be used and not read out

stranger.what: a key nothing here was wrapped by or for

rules.how: What every device holds a temporary camera to, whatever it is told: it lasts a day from Approve, each "Keep another day" adds a day, and it never lasts longer than a week from its start; a camera invite is good for ten minutes.

device_id.how: A temporary camera's device id is its key's, and nobody's to choose: the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 of "petcam.tempcam.id.v1|" followed by the 65 raw bytes of its public key (X9.63 uncompressed), with the version set to 8 (byte 6: its low four bits, then 0x80) and the variant to RFC 9562's (byte 8: its low six bits, then 0x80), written as a lowercase UUID. The server mints it so at registration; a member shows a code for a page, and takes a camera from a row, only where the id is the key's; and the page takes no pass under another.

cases.what: what it would be for another key

an_apps.how: An app takes for itself, when it registers (POST /v1/devices), only an id that is a random one: a version 4 UUID, RFC 9562's variant, lowercase, as every id the Worker picks is. Any other and it keeps nothing of the answer and isn't registered. A temporary camera's id is version 8, so no app ever holds an id a page could have, whoever answers its registration.

version 4 with another variant than RFC 9562's
uppercase: every id on the wire is lowercase

models.how: What a temporary camera's page can tell its device is: its `model` when it registers, and what it's called until a member names it. The Worker keeps any `model` of 64 characters, as for every device, so an app shows a `web` device's only when it is one of `known`, exactly; for anything else it shows its own word.

how: A temporary camera's name is a member's to give, at Approve and whenever someone renames it: {"name": "…"} sealed as any message (0x04) with the home's box key, for "petcam.tempcam.name.v1|<camera id>", where a device's name is sealed for "petcam.name.v1|<device id>". It opens only under the home's current keys.

A row with the mark (`temporary`) has its name opened as a temporary camera's, and every other row as a device's: never both. So the name a home gave one of its devices doesn't open on a temporary camera's row, whatever id that row has, nor the other way. `rows` has both, and `alert` the same for an offline alert's `camera_name`.
`with` is whose keys open: a holder (the home's keys, as that device holds them), or "camera", the page's own.

as_a_devices.what: The same words sealed as a device's name is, for the same id

a_members.what: The name the home gave one of its own cameras

camera.how: The camera's own keys: HKDF(secret, info) for each info, as an epoch's secret gives the home's (keys-v1.json). Nothing else is ever derived from a camera's secret: it has no join token, vouches for no key and proves no chain.

contexts.how: Associated data: UTF-8, never sent. The first two are sealed with the home's box key; the pass's is HPKE's; the rest are today's contexts, under the camera's keys when the camera in them is a temporary one.

invite.sealed_token_how: {"token": the token's base64url text, "expires_at": when it ends by its maker's clock (ms), ten minutes after it was made, "kind": "camera"}, sealed under the current epoch's box key for "petcam.caminvite.v1|" + invite id. A member invite's is {"token", "expires_at"} for "petcam.invite.v1|" + invite id, and names no kind.

tokens.how: What a device makes of a listed invite's `sealed_token`, opened as `holder` for `invite_id`: `kind` is "camera" (approving it hands over a pass), "member" (the home's keys) or null (nothing: no code, no approval). The context it opens under decides; the kind inside has to agree. `a_build_from_before` is what a build from before temporary cameras makes of the same bytes: it knows only a member's context and passes over a field it doesn't know.

request.how: The page asks as any device does (invite-v1.json): it commits to a nonce, proves it holds the link, a member answers with a nonce from the home's keys, and both show the code.

listing.how: A camera invite as the server lists it (GET /v1/household/invites) to a device holding `holder`'s keys at `now`. `kind` is by what was sealed, never the listing's own word; `code` is the request's as for a camera invite and `approvable` the same unless another request shows it too; `code_as_a_members` is what the same listing gives read as a member invite, which a camera's never does.

sealed.how: What the camera and the home's devices say to each other, under the camera's keys: messages are 0x04 || epoch || nonce || ciphertext || tag under its box key, its stills 0x05 || … under its media key, both naming the home's epoch when it started, and an offer's and an answer's `sig` is HMAC under its signal key. `with` says who opens: "camera" (the camera's keys: the page's, and a member's from its entry), "home" (the home's current keys), "another_camera" (another secret) or "camera_at_epoch_2" (this secret held as another epoch's).

watch.what: A signal from a viewer to the camera: a watch, saying what the calling device is called, for the camera's own screen

offer.what: A signal from the camera to that viewer: its offer, signed with the camera's signal key

answer.what: The viewer's answer, signed with the camera's signal key too

watch_without_the_relay.what: A watch from a viewer whose Relay switch is off: the camera sets this session up with no relay either. A page has no switch of its own, so a watch alone decides

offer_without_the_relay.what: The camera's offer for that session: it says it has no relay, and is signed as any offer is, since `relay` is outside what `sig` covers

bye_relay_off.what: The camera ending a session made without the relay whose path turned out relayed all the same

status_cannot_see.what: Its status while its page is hidden

command_peek.what: A command to it: stills for a grid tile, one second of them

command_keep.what: A command to it: more time, with its new end

command_end.what: A command to it: stop, and be gone

command_end_under_the_homes_keys.what: The same command sealed with the home's box key, as one to a member's camera is

commands.how: The only commands a member sends a temporary camera are `takes`: stills for a grid tile, more time, and stop. It does nothing for any other name, so a member seals no other for one, and a viewer offers nothing on a temporary camera that would send one: no Flip, zoom, light, night light, Pause, quality, sound, turning the picture, or detection setting. `never_sent` is every other command an app's camera takes, and one no build knows.

relay.how: The Relay switch (docs/API.md, Realtime) with a temporary camera. A viewer whose switch is off says `"relay": false` in its `watch`, sealed under the camera's keys as any signal to it is; a page has no switch of its own, so a watch alone decides. For such a watch the camera makes the session with no TURN server, lets none of the viewer's relay candidates in, and says `"relay": false` in its offer, whose `sig` is the same as without it: `relay` is outside what `sig` covers. A session whose selected path is relayed all the same ends with a `bye` whose reason is `relay_off`. `relay` is only ever said as false: missing, the side that sent it has the relay (`has_relay`).

status_reads.how: What a member reads of a temporary camera's status: `fields`, and nothing else of what it carries. What a viewer offers on a temporary camera goes by its entry, never by its status, so a page that says it has a back camera, a zoom range or a light is offered no more than one that doesn't. `of` names a status in `messages`; `reads` is what a member has of it.

signatures.how: base64url(HMAC(the camera's petcam.signal.v1 key, UTF-8 of session + "|" + kind + "|" + sdp)), the SDP exactly as it is sent. Both ends sign with the camera's key: the camera its offer, the viewer its answer.

how: A temporary camera makes no events, so its only alert is the offline one any camera brings (docs/API.md, Push payloads). The push says its camera is a temporary one: `temporary` true beside the rest as APNs carries it, and "true" in FCM's data, where every value is text. A device then opens `camera_name` as a temporary camera's name; in a push that doesn't say so, as a device's. Never both.

`user_info` is the push as an Apple device gets it and `fcm.data` the same as an Android one does, with the `tag` it posts the notification under; `holder` the keys the device holds. `alert` is what it writes: the camera's name where it opens under the current keys, else its own "Pet Cam Pro", and its own words for a camera that went offline. `ahead`: the name is sealed under keys newer than the device holds, so it catches up on the home's keys first.

cases.name: offline
cases.why: a temporary camera went offline: the push says it is one, and its name opens as a temporary camera's

cases.name: not_said_to_be_temporary
cases.why: the same name in a push that doesn't say so: it's opened as a device's, and doesn't open

cases.name: a_devices_name_said_to_be_temporary
cases.why: one of the home's own cameras, with the name the home gave it, in a push that says it's a temporary camera: opened as a temporary camera's, and it doesn't open

cases.name: a_devices_alert
cases.why: the same camera's alert as the server sends one for any device: nothing changed for those

cases.name: no_name
cases.why: a temporary camera nobody named

cases.name: after_a_key_change
cases.why: the home has moved on: a name opens only under the current keys

cases.name: under_newer_keys
cases.why: sealed under keys the device hasn't caught up on: it catches up first, and these are the words if it can't

rows.how: A device as the server lists it to a member that knows temporary cameras (GET /v1/me, device_updated). `marked` is whether the row carries the mark (`temporary`); `takes`, whether a device holding `holder`'s keys at `now` has a camera in it: the entry in the mark opens for this device's id under its current keys, the id is the entry's key's, and neither the entry's end nor the server's sooner one has come. `opens_name` is what the row's name reads as, a camera or not: a temporary camera's on a row with the mark, a device's on any other, null where it doesn't open. `called` is what a row with the mark is called in a list: that name, else its `model` where it is one a page says (`models`), else null, for which an app has a word of its own; never a plain name or a model as the server gave them. `reads` is then what a member shows of a camera: that name, its end (the sooner of the two), who started it, and `viewers` from its status, opened with the keys its entry gives.

cases.name: a_temporary_camera
cases.why: role camera, platform web, and the mark: its entry opens under the home's current keys for this device, it isn't past its end, and its status opens with the keys its entry gives. Its name is a member's, sealed with the home's box key under a context of its own.

cases.name: given_another_day
cases.why: the entry a member sealed again with a day more, an hour after it would have ended

cases.name: the_servers_end_is_sooner
cases.why: the server's copy of its end can only make the end sooner: the sooner of the two counts

cases.name: past_the_servers_end
cases.why: at the server's sooner end: over

cases.name: the_servers_end_is_later
cases.why: the server says it has a month left: its sealed end is what counts, and it's past that

cases.name: past_its_end
cases.why: at its sealed end, by this device's own clock: not a camera any more, whatever the server lists

cases.name: its_entry_on_another_device
cases.why: the entry moved to another device's row: it doesn't open there, and nor does the name

cases.name: after_a_key_change
cases.why: the home has moved on: a key change ended it

cases.name: marked_with_no_entry
cases.why: marked, with no entry: only the home's own word makes a camera of it

cases.name: a_browser_with_no_mark
cases.why: platform web with no mark: nothing the home's devices watch or hand anything to. No member vouched for its key, so nothing that hands out the home's keys counts it. Its name, a temporary camera's, doesn't open on a row without the mark.

cases.name: a_members_camera
cases.why: a member's camera has no mark: everything to and from it is under the home's keys, and its name opens as any device's

cases.name: in_a_members_cameras_place
cases.why: the page's entry, sealed for the id of one of the home's own cameras, on that camera's row with that camera's name: the entry opens there, and the id isn't the key's, so no member takes it; and the name the home gave that camera doesn't open on a row with the mark. Without the two, a server and a page could put made-up pictures in a real camera's place, under its name.

cases.name: named_as_a_device
cases.why: a temporary camera whose name was sealed as a device's is: it is a camera, and that name doesn't open, so it is called what its page says it is

cases.name: a_members_camera_named_as_a_temporary_one
cases.why: one of the home's own cameras whose name was sealed as a temporary camera's is: that name doesn't open on a row without the mark

cases.name: a_plain_name_from_the_server
cases.why: a temporary camera nobody named, on a row where the server wrote a plain name (`legacy_name`, which a device's own row carried before names were sealed): it is called what its page says it is, never the server's word

cases.name: a_model_from_the_server
cases.why: a temporary camera nobody named, whose model isn't one a page says: the app's own word for one, never the server's
